key_insight: A normal form for Pauli-based computation fully characterizes its adaptivity and entanglement, linking it to one-way quantum computing as a time-reversed counterpart.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports ahead-of-time compilation and distributed quantum computation while reducing gate and quantum-memory requirements.
method: Derive a normal form for the adaptive and entanglement structures of Pauli-based computation.
Use it to study distributed computation and magic-state injection rates.
Efficiently detect and remove unnecessary magic-state qubits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average reductions of 50% in CNOT count and 40% in quantum memory for random quantum circuits, outperforming other state-of-the-art compilers.
watch_item: Results on random circuits may not generalize to practical workloads; hardware-level benefits require validation under connectivity, noise, and measurement constraints.
paper_title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
